state.misconception_label: Thinks alternate angles are always equal

turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are arguing about alternate angles. Tom says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are alternate. Katie says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are equal. Who is correct? ![Shows two non parallel lines that are intersected by another line. Angles P and Q are both on the outside of the lines and on opposite sides of the transversal.](). I got Only
Katie because I assumed all the angles in the figure are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me explain the correct method, and then we will work through an example together. Can you tell me what alternate angles are supposed to be?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, I think alternate angles are the ones that are on opposite sides of the transversal, right? But I thought they were always equal no matter what. So, if they’re not always equal, when are they equal then?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Alternate angles are indeed the ones on opposite sides of the transversal, but they are not always equal. Alternate angles are equal only when the lines intersected by the transversal are parallel. Let's work through an example to clarify this concept.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, so if alternate angles are equal only when the lines are parallel, how can I tell if the lines are parallel just by looking at the angles? And what if they’re not parallel—does that mean the alternate angles can be different?
